profile.headline: Software Engineer at Galoy
profile.summary:
Senior Backend Engineer specializing in low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems — Kotlin and Java, on a Credit, Fraud & Risk decisioning platform processing $1B+ in loan originations.

I build the systems that make real-time decisions under load. At Jenius Bank (SMBC), I re-architected a loan-orchestration pipeline on Kotlin and AKS — parallelizing IO-bound credit-bureau calls to cut P90 decision latency from ~6s to ~2s — and designed a unified, version-routed decision API that scaled one decisioning core across three product lines without breaking existing integrations. I also built an in-house, configuration-driven rules engine that migrated threshold-based decisioning off a vendor platform and cut those vendor costs ~30%.
Before fintech, I built backend services for FedEx's dynamic-pricing platform (Java/Spring Boot) and architected its cloud-migration messaging layer, and started my career as a security analyst shipping production Python — so I bring a security-aware lens to backend work.

What I care about: clean service boundaries, systems that stay fast and reliable under real traffic, and architecture decisions that hold up as the product grows.

Stack: Kotlin · Java · Spring Boot · microservices · gRPC/REST · distributed systems · decision engines · Azure · AKS / Kubernetes · Docker · Cosmos DB · Redis · CI/CD

Open to Senior Backend / Platform / Software Engineer roles.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Credit and fraud risk decisioning platform spanning loans, savings, and external account linking, processing $1B+ in loan originations. Loan onboarding — the highest-volume, most complex flow — has been my primary focus.
• Re-architected the loan-orchestration layer in Kotlin on AKS, pulling bureau orchestration out of a single-threaded vendor engine so IO-bound credit-bureau calls run in parallel — cutting P90 decision latency from ~6s to ~2s.
• Proposed and drove adoption of a unified loan-decision API that routes to the correct rule flow by the credit-strategy version passed at request time — winning buy-in from a skeptical, risk-averse senior stakeholder over a competing plan to duplicate the codebase per product line.
• Established an immutable, additive rule-versioning model (existing rules never modified, only added; thresholds become parameters; rules compose into per-version flows) so new lending rules can't break existing product integrations — eliminating a class of regression defects.
• Built a configuration-driven, in-house rules engine — rules encoded as versioned CSV definitions executed by a custom parser/engine — to migrate threshold-based decisioning off the Provenir vendor platform, cutting vendor cost ~30% for those rule sets.
• Cut vendor decisioning costs further by re-sequencing bureau calls into gated stages — running TransUnion and LexisNexis rules first, calling income/fraud providers (TWN, SoCure) only when the first stage passes.
• Technical lead for the loan-top-ups build: owned architecture and requirements for a team of three (two mid-level engineers, one new grad), decomposed and assigned the work, reviewed all code, and shipped to production.
• Architected the decisioning data layer on Cosmos DB (MongoDB API) with Redis for hot-path reads, and partnered with Product and Risk/Compliance to enforce TILA disclosures, fair-lending constraints, and adverse-action handling directly in the decisioning flow.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Key Achievement: Architected and delivered a mission-critical dynamic-pricing microservice, directly contributing to a 15% increase in revenue predictability.

Microservices & Cloud Migration: Led the transition from legacy ActiveMQ messaging to a modern, event-driven architecture using Azure Event Grid and Azure Storage. This eliminated cross-team dependencies and significantly accelerated the feature development lifecycle.

DevOps & Cost Optimization: Engineered ephemeral test environments, enabling on-demand provisioning for the engineering team. This initiative slashed infrastructure costs by 40% and reduced environment-related bottlenecks.

Security & Authentication: Hardened the service’s security posture by implementing OAuth 2.0 for all internal app-to-app communications. This ensured secure, authenticated interactions across service boundaries and safeguarded critical workflows.

System Performance: Refactored core Java Spring Boot components and designed scalable database schemas to support evolving business requirements, ensuring high performance and long-term maintainability.

Agile Delivery: Collaborated with cross-functional teams to translate complex business logic into scalable technical solutions, consistently delivering features ahead of schedule.

positions.title: Cyber Security Analyst
positions.description:
- Led the revitalization of the Wi-Fi Intrusion Prevention System at FedEx, enhancing the security of locations across North America. This project involved deep network security knowledge and proactive defense strategies against potential cyber threats.

- Assisted in automating the synchronization of workload labels between ServiceNow CMDB and the Illumio micro segmentation tool using Python scripting. This crucial process ensured accurate label information for micro segmentation rules, enhancing system security and efficiency.

- Contributed to a Proof of Concept (POC) for Secure Private Access solutions to modernize and enhance secure remote access, leading to the selection and successful implementation of Zscaler across FedEx.

- Conducted thorough reviews of company projects to ensure compliance with established cybersecurity standards, including the evaluation of network diagrams and security protocols.
positions.insights: Python (Programming Language), Domain Name System (DNS) and +3 skills

positions.title: Cyber Security Intern
positions.description: - Strategically collaborated with external vendors to execute and assess proof of concept tests for advanced anomaly detection tools in the OT environment, gaining critical insights into integrating enhanced security measures within software systems.
